c73dca1b-c179-593d-9ff2-c9e643811ee8.name: Abu Radan Dress
c73dca1b-c179-593d-9ff2-c9e643811ee8.description: Black dress with wide, open sleeves, made from cotton fabric with heavy embroidery. The chest panel shows geometrical motifs (fans) on a rose-coloured collar. The shoulders show an embroidered emblem that is known as *nishan*, and the sleeves are heavily embroidered with cypress trees and waves that include yellow braid work along the length of the sleeve. The side panels of the dress (*banayeq*) show braid work with floral motifs topped by a scissor motif (*maqas*). The lower front panel of the dress shows motifs of cypress branches in different colours. The back shows the Pasha’s tent motif bordered by geometrical figures and cypress branches, while the bottom edge of the back panel has two blue lines that go around the dress. This type of dress was used mainly for celebrations and was worn by unmarried women only for events like weddings and women-only parties. These dresses were produced by hand by the same women who wore them, thus demonstrating the female’s ability to be productive. The origins of this dress lie in Bir al-Sabe, which is one of the largest cities in Palestine and is also known as the capital of the Negev desert. Some Bir al-Sabe inhabitants are originally Bedouin tribes, which explains why the women of Bir al-Sabe used to wear these heavy dresses. The garment has the advantage of being heavy, which helps the wearer cope with the desert climate in that region; it prevents sand from entering the women’s bodies and protects them from the heat. The dress is only worn by the women of Bir al-Sabe, and it is unique to them in respect of all the colours, stitches and motifs that the dress exhibits. It is worth mentioning that while Palestinian traditional costumes are distinguished by their individuality and regionalism, they still exhibit the influence of the different stages of occupation that Palestine has witnessed throughout its long history. In this case, the Ottoman influence is reflected in the long sleeves of the dress.
